segments.text: Hook: Marian Rejewski broke Enigma in 1932 by applying permutation theory and exploiting German procedural flaws.
Using data from French spies who had intercepted daily keys, he solved the rotor wiring.
He was joined by Jerzy Różycki and Henryk Zygalski, who built Enigma doubles and developed the cyclometer, cataloguing 100,000 entries, and the Zygalski sheets.
When Germany added more rotors in 1938, the Poles expanded their equipment to keep up.
Payoff: Their work laid the groundwork for all later decryption efforts.
